atoms.title: Caribbean Culture in the US : Jamaican Food

atoms.text: The first Black people who lived in the United States were enslaved people taken from Africa. Today, their descendants make up the majority of the Black population in the US Yet, many Black Americans have other heritage. Some have recently immigrated from Africa, others are second or third-generation immigrants. Some have roots in Latin America and others have Caribbean heritage, such as Jamaican Americans.

atoms.text: Jamaicans have had a presence in the US for centuries, but the bulk of migration from Jamaica has taken place since the turn of the 20th century. Most Jamaican Americans reside in South Florida and New York City. In those two regions, they have had a great cultural impact. There are plenty of famous Americans with Jamaican roots including the 49th Vice President Kamala Harris, whose father was born on the island. Jamaicans who moved to the US brought elements of their culture with them, including their cuisine, which they then shared with other Americans. Today, one can find Jamaican food in most cities in the US

text: Jamaica is an island in the Caribbean Sea. It is about 700 miles south of Florida.
hint.sound: Jamaica is an island in the Caribbean Sea. It is about 700 miles south of Florida.
hint.label: Jamaica

atoms.text: Jamaica, like the United States, has a history of colonialism, slavery and immigration, causing the country to be a blend of many cultures. This history can be seen in its food. Through their blend of spices and preparation methods, popular culinary dishes reflect all the cultures that have shaped Jamaica. The Taino, the original inhabitants of the island, cultivated the root vegetable cassava, which is still used in Jamaican cooking. The influence of Indian immigrants can be seen especially in the use of curry in Jamaica. One of the most popular dishes on the island is curried goat. In addition, many fruits and vegetables originally from West Africa are used in Jamaican cooking. These include ackee, the national fruit, pictured above. Ackee and saltfish (salted cod) is the national dish of Jamaica.
atoms.sound: Jamaica, like the United States, has a history of colonialism, slavery and immigration, causing the country to be a blend of many cultures. This history can be seen in its food. Through their blend of spices and preparation methods, popular culinary dishes reflect all the cultures that have shaped Jamaica. The Thai-ino, the original inhabitants of the island, cultivated the root vegetable cassava, which is still used in Jamaican cooking. The influence of Indian immigrants can be seen especially in the use of curry in Jamaica.  One of the most popular dishes on the island is curried goat. In addition, many fruits and vegetables originally from West Africa are used in Jamaican cooking. These include ackee, the national fruit, pictured above. Ackee and saltfish, (salted cod), is the national dish of Jamaica.

atoms.text: Unlike Jamaica, not all regions of the US are tropical. Therefore, even though Jamaican food has become popular in the States, different dishes are favoured for practical purposes. While ackee and cod are harder to come by in places like New York, people prepare jerk chicken on the streets of Brooklyn in the traditional Jamaican way. “Jerk” is a Jamaican style of cooking in which meat is marinated with a blend of hot spices and then cooked over coal. Patties, a pastry filled with spiced meat, are also beloved across the United States.
